questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

5 6 In order to maximise his utility, which quantities of X and Y should the consumer purchase? X Y
Firms can grow internally or externally. Which strategy is an example of a commercial bank growing internally?

options.A: the bank cutting its costs by rationalising its structure
options.B: the bank merging with another commercial bank
options.D: the bank taking over an insurance company

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s cost and revenue curves. MC cost / AC revenue MR AR O output The firm changes its objective from sales revenue maximisation to profit maximisation. How will this affect the net economic welfare of the following groups in the short run? customers workers

options.A: fall rise

questions.questionText: A market structure in which a small number of firms face competition from potential entrants. What does this describe?

options.A: a contestable market

questions.questionText: At its current level of output, a monopolist is on the price-inelastic part of its demand curve. What will be the effect of an increase in the price charged by the firm on its output and on its profits? output profits

options.A: decrease increase

questions.questionText: A country has a negative tax income regime. The curve NT in the diagram shows the country’s initial tax schedule. + NT tax NT O income –

options.A: strengthen less equal

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for new cars. Currently the quantity supplied is fixed by the government at S . S S x y price z w D O quantity If the market was deregulated the supply curve would be S . Which area measures the net welfare gain of removing the restriction on the quantity supplied?

options.A: w + y B x + y C z + w D z + x + y + w

questions.questionText: What are the losses in economic efficiency that are likely to result from a policy of income redistribution from the rich to the poor? distortion of individual administrative costs disincentive choices between work of the redistribution effects and leisure policy

options.A: yes yes no

questions.questionText: A government regulates the price charged by a monopolist. In which circumstance will such intervention improve economic efficiency?

options.A: The government sets the price where average revenue equals marginal cost.
options.B: The government sets the price where marginal cost is below average cost.
options.C: The intervention results in an increase in producer surplus.
options.D: The intervention results in predatory pricing.

questions.questionText: How are the weights applied to the different indicators used to construct the United Nations’ Human Development Index determined?

options.A: by the amount a country falls short of the maximum value of each indicator
options.B: by the proportion of GNP a country devotes to promoting each of the indicators
options.C: by the relative importance attached to the different indicators by the United Nations
options.D: by the relative size of each country’s population

questions.questionText: Which assets are included within the definition of broad money but not within the definition of narrow money?

options.A: commercial banks’ deposits at the central bank

questions.questionText: When national income equals $30000 million and government spending equals $15000 million, an economy is in equilibrium below full employment. Out of every increase of $100 in national income, $10 is taken in taxes, $25 is spent on imports and $15 is saved. To raise national income to the full employment level of $50000 million, to which level will the government need to raise its own spending?

options.A: $20000 million

questions.questionText: In a banking system, all banks maintain 20% of deposits as cash. One bank receives a new cash deposit of $200. Subsequent net withdrawals of cash from the banking system are zero. What will be the resulting increase in bank loans and the total increase in bank deposits? increase in total increase bank loans in deposits $ $

A government finances an increase in spending by selling government securities to foreign residents. What will be the immediate effect on the money supply and on the foreign exchange reserves? foreign exchange money supply reserves

options.A: decrease decrease

questions.questionText: What will cause a fall in the quantity of money demanded?

options.A: a rise in interest rates
options.C: a rise in the price level

questions.questionText: The table gives the growth rate of nominal GDP, the population growth rate and the rate of inflation in one year for four countries. Which country had the greatest growth in average living standards? nominal GDP growth population growth rate rate of inflation rate % % %
When might an increase in a government budget deficit be considered the most appropriate policy?

options.A: when inflation is high
options.B: when there is a balance of payments trade deficit
options.C: when there is high cyclical unemployment
options.D: when there is high structural unemployment

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the relationship between the rate of increase in wages and the rate of unemployment. rate of increase in wages O rate of unemployment What would be likely to cause the curve in the diagram to shift downwards and to the left?

options.A: an increase in regional differences in unemployment rates
options.B: an increase in the proportion of the workforce belonging to trade unions
options.C: an increase in the unemployment rate
options.D: the expectation of a lower rate of inflation

questions.questionText: The diagram shows details of the British Government’s estimated spending and receipts for 2010–2011. All figures in UK £bn. spending receipts health national welfare income tax insurance 226 150 99 total: education total: £697 89 £548 VAT billion billion 81 debt other interest 79 excise duties 44 46 other defence council tax 114 40 corporation tax law and business housing & 43 order rates environment 35 25 What can be concluded from the diagram? effect of largest type of largest overall budget spending item on receipt item balance income distribution

options.A: less equitable indirect tax deficit

questions.questionText: What do governments need to do to allow automatic stabilisers to work?

options.A: adjust taxes in order to achieve a balanced budget
options.B: keep welfare benefit rates and tax rates unchanged
options.C: lower both taxes and government expenditure in a slump
options.D: lower taxes in a boom and raise taxes in a slump

questions.questionText: What is not a supply-side policy measure?

options.A: deregulating industry to encourage more competitive markets
options.B: linking unemployment benefits to the obligation to look for work
options.C: tackling cyclical unemployment by lowering interest rates
options.D: tackling structural unemployment by giving grants for labour mobility

questions.questionText: A country has a fixed exchange rate. Which combination of problems would be most likely to cause the country’s government to reduce taxation and lower interest rates?

options.A: demand inflation and a balance of payments current account deficit
options.B: demand inflation and a low level of investments
options.C: high unemployment and a balance of payments current account deficit
options.D: high unemployment and a low level of investment

questions.questionText: An economy has a low level of unemployment. The government increases its expenditure. Which method of financing the additional expenditure is most likely to cause inflation?

options.A: an increase in borrowing from the Central Bank
options.C: an increase in sales of state assets to the non-bank private sector
